summary:
Lane "consistency" is complete. Files: notes.md (long text) and result.json (keys conflicts, packages, compatibility, notes, differs, settled) in /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round2/consistency/. The repository was read only (git status is the same as at the start). No request went to production. Remote: origin https://github.com/ariakit/visonaut.git. Skills loaded: ariakit-general-workflow, ariakit-general-code-style, ariakit-ariakit-api-design.

Count correction: the task says 45 clean selections. The feedback gives 49 selections; without D-DATA-02 and D-WORK-04 that is 47 (42 with no note, plus D-LOAD-01, D-LOAD-04, D-CODE-05, D-CODE-04, D-WORK-02). result.json has settledAnswer and rationale for all 47 (1 or 2 sentences, and 1 to 3 sentences; a build check enforces the limits and the option ids).

1. Conflicts and order: 18 items (C01 to C18) and 9 packages (P0 to P8; each of the 47 decisions is in exactly one package). Four items need a word of the maintainer before work starts:
- C01: three fixes of accepted lists add D1 writes against the standing rule: 6 new indexes (D-DATA-01), the table pull_request_titles (D-DATA-01), and a heartbeat row for each pass, 288 each day (D-OPS-01 row 8). Three selected options add writes too: D-DATA-04 (deletes), D-AUTH-05 (one UPDATE one time), D-AUTH-03 (a rare new review session row). Measured on local D1: an INSERT writes 1, 2, 3 rows with 0, 1, 2 indexes. The new column of D-RUN-02 adds no written row. The settled text of D-DATA-01 and D-OPS-01 says that these rows wait.
- C04: five answers repair the queued save path (D-RES-02, D-RUN-05, D-RES-01 row 6, D-OPS-01 row 12, D-RUN-01 REVIEW-07), and D-RES-05 is open because of it. The server has a direct save path with no caller (apps/web/src/api/review.ts:879-904) that returns the reviewer and no model. The task row of one queued decision writes 13 rows (local measurement). With no-promise, the maintainer can look at the queue again. Not settled.
- C08: D-WORK-03 keeps the keys, and D-WORK-02 adds swipe and overlay, which must have keys by the note. The two letters are not selected. The preload of D-RUN-01 must cover 3 images.
- C11: the record stores the pull request title in two ways (a new table in D-DATA-01, 'no new table' in D-UX-04). A third form keeps the title in the webhook payload in the UPDATE that exists: 0 more written rows, no migration.
Other main items: D-LOAD-04 and D-LOAD-05 are one loader (the D-LOAD-05 sketch has ssr: false); with D-UX-02 the layout route must not have ssr: false (documented, and confirmed in the installed router-core 1.170.38); fixes of D-LOAD-01 and D-UX-01 are written for the URLs of today and D-UX-02 replaces them; the run page needs a navigation blocker when its header gets router links; the check text of D-OPS-07, the words of D-UX-03, and the result page of D-WORK-05 need one count definition (the lab found 17 or 18 against 15), and the D-WORK-05 example text 'The visual check passed' conflicts with row 14 of D-OPS-01; D-UI-02 comes before D-UI-03, and row 3 of D-UI-01 is replaced by D-UI-03; seven changes edit deploy.yml and wrangler.jsonc; each CLI change is a cutover whose cost D-OPS-04 sets, so one release must hold all of them.

2. No backward compatibility: 17 places (K01 to K17) and 7 places where the rule is not safe (N1 to N7). Key fact: production has a new database since 2026-10-04 that holds only the project configuration and the imported baseline as an inventory (docs/baseline-delta-cutover.md:3), so most old forms that the code reads are probably not in production (assumption; nobody read production). Selected answers to look at again: D-UX-02 (the /?view= redirect), D-RUN-02 (the fallback read for older runs), D-CODE-02 (three steps), D-OPS-01 rows 1, 9, 13 (code for old checks), D-RES-01 and D-AUTH-01 (contract line 83 freezes answer codes; /api/me and the bearer plugin stay only because old records and a README name them; the Ariakit workflows call only 'visonaut submit'), D-CODE-05 (the seed of today builds the legacy storage form). Not safe: decisions since 2026-10-04, the baseline, active runs, the GitHub check contract, the pin between the two repositories, applied migrations with one trigger.

3. Three notes: D-LOAD-04: the maintainer is right. The TanStack Start documentation describes route loaders (isomorphic), deferred promises, and a streamed document; the head request is a hand-written script. The audit recommended it for risk (a second path to private data with 5 rules), not for idiom. result.json lists 9 needs, the main ones: return the promise without await, call the /api/runs handler in the same process so that D-LOAD-03 applies one time, no cookie renewal in a streamed response, ssr 'data-only' for the dates, and one test of a return to the queue with a deferred loader. D-CODE-05: right for D1 and R2 (local state in .wrangler/state, d1 migrations apply --local, d1 execute --local, r2 object put --local; flags confirmed in the installed Wrangler 4.136.1). The signed session and the GitHub answers are not Wrangler features. D-CODE-04: 329 files, 8,317,186 bytes, 99,041 words move to docs/history/; 5 files with 12,242 words stay; 368 links cross the border (78 + 24 + 266); 3 code paths read moved files; contract-issue-1.md (10,240 words) is binding by contract line 7 and needs the maintainer's word.

4. Rationale with numbers for D-LOAD-04, D-OPS-07, D-OPS-05, D-WORK-03, D-DATA-04, D-CODE-05, D-CODE-04, D-WORK-06, D-RES-02 is in result.json under "differs" (gives, costs, watch).

recommendations.decision: Order of work for the 47 settled decisions
recommendations.option: P0 facts and open answers, P1 documents, P2 service fixes, P3 deploy and Worker, P4 run data, P5 routes and loaders, P6 UI system, P7 review workspace, P8 one CLI and adapter release
recommendations.reason: Each package starts only after what it needs: the history moves before 76 contract links and the contract edits change; the access check of D-LOAD-03 exists before the server read of D-LOAD-04; D-RUN-02 gives the small response that D-RUN-05, D-RES-03, and D-WORK-05 need; D-UI-02 gives the Heading that D-UI-03 needs; all CLI changes go into one release because each release is a cutover with a measured failure window of 34 to 41 minutes.
recommendations.wrongIf: D-DATA-02 or D-OPS-04 get an answer that needs no format change or no cutover, or the maintainer wants the visible UI work (P6, P7) before the server work.

recommendations.decision: C11: where the pull request title is stored (D-DATA-01 and D-UX-04 disagree)
recommendations.option: keep the title in the webhook payload in the UPDATE that exists
recommendations.reason: It adds 0 written rows (measured locally: the settle UPDATE writes 1 row with and without the title), no table, and no migration, and the two readers and the index of today work. The title table adds 1 written row for each pull_request webhook.
recommendations.wrongIf: The maintainer wants the processed payload empty for capacity or privacy, or the 5 statements that write '{}' cannot be changed together (a restore then erases the titles).

recommendations.decision: C01: what the rule 'no increase of D1 writes' means for the new indexes and the heartbeat
recommendations.reason: The evidence gives the cost of each side (1 more written row for each index on each insert; one written row is priced as 1,000 rows read; the indexes remove about 600,000 rows read for one statement in a projected state, and near zero today), but the rule is the maintainer's. The settled text of D-DATA-01 and D-OPS-01 holds these rows until the answer.
recommendations.wrongIf: Not applicable: this is a question for the maintainer.

recommendations.decision: C04: keep the durable decision queue after D-RES-02 (no-promise), or use the direct save path
recommendations.reason: The direct path exists (review.ts:879-904), writes 13 fewer rows for each decision in the local measurement, needs no poll, and returns the reviewer that D-RES-05 misses. It gives up admission in one short request and a decision that survives a closed tab. Nobody measured the time of a direct save in production, so the evidence supports no recommendation.
recommendations.wrongIf: Not applicable: flag for the maintainer. A production timing of one save would support a recommendation.

recommendations.decision: D-LOAD-04 and D-LOAD-05: how the two selected answers become one design
recommendations.option: one loader: on the server it calls the /api/runs handler in the same process and returns its promise; in the browser it fetches /api/runs
recommendations.reason: A route has one loader. One endpoint keeps one access check (the 2 round trips of D-LOAD-03), the status rules, and the origin check, and it is the smallest form of the 'separately scoped authenticated server read' of P03. The documentation describes loaders as isomorphic and deferred promises as the way to stream.
recommendations.wrongIf: A small build shows that a deferred loader shows the loading text again on a return to the queue (then the loader must await in the browser), or the measured gap after D-LOAD-01 to D-LOAD-03 is too small to pay for effort M.

recommendations.option: docs/history/ keeps the layout of docs/ (docs/history/evidence, docs/history/simplification-audit, docs/history/operations, and the top-level records)
recommendations.reason: A link between two moved files then does not change. Only the 368 links that cross the border change, and the move can be one commit that changes paths only.
recommendations.wrongIf: The maintainer wants contract-issue-1.md (binding by contract line 7) or the one-time SQL files beside the current guides, or wants a flat history folder.

recommendations.decision: D-UX-02: the redirect of old /?view= links
recommendations.reason: The redirect exists only for bookmarks. 10 organization members can sign in and 5 have push permission, and the maintainer said that backward compatibility is not necessary. The two link shapes that GitHub checks store are not old URLs and stay.
recommendations.wrongIf: A tool or a document that the maintainer uses opens /?view=history or /?view=service.

recommendations.option: measure one review read again before the build of D-RUN-03
recommendations.reason: After D-RUN-02 and D-RUN-05 the inventory read stays only for the unchanged list and for Submit, so the measured gain (680 to 225 ms locally) no longer applies to a first load or to a save, and the option changes a tested trust rule at effort M. D-DATA-02 can also replace the reader.
recommendations.wrongIf: The production trace shows that the unchanged list is opened in most reviews and its read is slow, or D-RUN-02 is built much later than D-RUN-03.

recommendations.decision: D-UI-01 row 3 (19 fixed pixel sizes written in rem)
recommendations.option: leave the row out and do D-UI-03 in its place
recommendations.reason: D-UI-03 (stock sizes and one base size) removes each fixed size, so the row is work that is done two times.
recommendations.wrongIf: D-UI-03 is built much later than the other rows of D-UI-01: the row then fixes the browser font size defect in the time between.

limits: Not checked: production (no request was sent; each statement about what production holds is from the cutover runbook and is an assumption). The D1 write counts are from the local D1 of Miniflare with the table and index definitions of the migrations, not from D1 in production, and they cover single statements, not a complete Submit or a complete decision. Nobody built the server loader, the head request, the local backend, or the docs move: the link count reads Markdown links only and does not find paths in HTML, JSON, or code comments. The return to the queue with a deferred loader was not tested. I did not verify if the response of a TanStack server function passes the securePrivateResponse wrapper, and I did not find or test a way to stub GitHub requests under the Cloudflare Vite plugin. The documentation quotes came through a fetch tool that summarizes pages, so each quote should be checked against the page before it goes into the record. The claim that the columns of D-UX-04 (closed reason) and D-AUTH-04 (settings count) can go into writes that exist is an assumption from the option texts, not from the code. I did not write record files (sections, decisions.json, terms.json): the settled text is in result.json for the merge. The open decisions D-DATA-02, D-OPS-04, D-WORK-04, and D-RES-05 belong to other lanes and are only referenced. The interactive design-document steps of the API design skill (page, tooltips, browser check) are the work of the merge step, not of this lane.
